messages:
maya: quick FYI — hit a burst of OOMs on gpu-pool during model boot for a customer. pattern: many small safetensors shards, NFS backend, heavy parallel warmup. reproducible on canary.
jin: saw same. logs show read spikes: thousands of small reads (~4–16KB) per shard, tons of metadata ops.
olga: NFS + small-file read amplification + page cache churn = bad. index-first approach makes us stat many files before streaming data.
sam: what if we shift to streaming first for initial layers + index-later for tail? avoids stat storm but loses quick random-access mapping.
maya: idea: compact sidecar manifest that lists per-shard contiguous byte ranges for the common path. smaller index, single seek, but still supports full index fallback. sidecar would be generated at model ingest.
jin: that would reduce syscall count a lot. we can include a "hotmask" bitset for high-priority layers so warmup can prioritize. also include checksum and format-version.
olga: tradeoffs: requires model ingest pipeline change and we need backwards compat. also if model vendor re-packs shards the sidecar could be stale. need manifest provenance (etag + signed manifest).
sam: operational concern: what about read-side backpressure? currently workers all prefetch aggressively and overwhelm NFS leading to eviction thrash. we need adaptive concurrency.
maya: propose two parts: (1) compact sidecar manifest as primary fast-path; (2) adaptive prefetch controller that rate-limits per-node based on instantaneous disk latency and page-fault rate.
jin: sketches — prefetch controller monitors mean read latency and OOM pressure signal. simple PID-ish limiter that reduces concurrent shard fetches when latency > 30ms. also use a token-bucket for bytes/s.
olga: eviction scoring needs to incorporate load-in-progress. if a shard is being fetched we should avoid evicting its neighbors to reduce wasted work. add state machine: FETCHING -> HOT -> COOL.
sam: can we compute a layer priority that blends usage and size? e.g., priority = usage_count * (1 / sqrt(size_mb)) + locality_bonus. That way small frequently-used layers bubble up.
jin: example pseudo in one line: `score(layer) = access_count * (1.0 / sqrt(size_mb)) + 0.5 * locality_hint` — we can tweak coefficients in runtime.
maya: security/provenance: sidecar should be signed by ingest service; runtime verifies before using compact fast-path. fallback: if sidecar missing or invalid, revert to existing index-first streaming.
jin: implementation notes: sidecar format = newline-delimited records: `layer_name byte_offset length hotbit checksum` — kept intentionally minimal. compress with zstd at ingest. expose a header with model-ETag and signed-hash.
olga: also need to expose telemetry: per-prefetch latencies, token-bucket fill, evict decisions exported to console so we can tune heuristics.
runtime-bot: deploy-check: ensure canary on dedicated pool only. "prefetch_controller" feature flag gated and off by default.
maya: action items: jin + olga to prototype sidecar writer and verifier (PR1), sam to add basic token-bucket limiter and latency probe (PR2). target: canary next week on gpu-dedicated. keep index-first fallback for safety.
sam: ack. will also add a quick hazard mitigation: if read-latency > 100ms for >10s, abort ongoing warmup and mark node as degraded to avoid cascading OOMs.
jin: noted. will add small test harness with NFS emulator to simulate metadata storms.
maya: thanks — leaving notes in the RFC follow-up doc. ping me on results. :thumbsup:
